name: Vocational training residence permit (Ausbildung, § 16a AufenthG)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a signed vocational training contract (Ausbildungsvertrag) with a recognised German training provider.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a signed Ausbildungsvertrag before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires German at B1 (B2 often preferred by training providers, though not always statutorily required).
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved German test at B1.

value.note: waived if the paid Ausbildung stipend is at least €992/month; otherwise blocked account or Verpflichtungserklärung required

requirements.blocker_text: This requires proof of funds of €11,904/year — waived if your Ausbildung stipend is at least €992/month.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm your stipend meets the threshold, or fund a blocked account.

evidence_required.document: Approved German test certificate at B1
Proof of funds or stipend confirmation

outcome.duration_length: 2 to 3.5 years, covering the training period

notes: Genuine cost-saving conditional worth surfacing prominently: most Ausbildung programs pay a stipend that clears the €992/month bar on its own, making the blocked-account requirement moot for most applicants — a real practical difference from de_student, where the blocked account is essentially always required. Part-time work up to 20 hours/week permitted outside the program, same cap as de_chancenkarte's side-work allowance — worth noting as a recurring German-system constant when comparing routes. After completion: feeds directly into de_job_seeker_post_study (18-month permit), then typically into de_eu_blue_card or a general skilled-worker permit once a qualified role is secured, with permanent residence realistically achievable after 2 years of qualified employment post-Ausbildung — faster than almost any other entry path in this dataset, though not modeled as a direct leads_to_pr here since the qualifying employment step is a genuinely separate route, not automatic.
